question: What was the child sex-ratio as per Census 2011 of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**919**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The child sex-ratio as per Census 2011 of India is **919 females per 1000 males**.
 
• The child sex-ratio is defined as the number of females per thousand males in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• This ratio is a crucial indicator of gender equality in a society and reflects the status of female children in the country.
 
• India's child sex-ratio has been a matter of concern due to the preference for male children in various parts of the country.
 
• The government has implemented several schemes and policies to address the imbalance and improve the status of the girl child.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Census of India is conducted every ten years and is the largest administrative exercise in the country.
 
• The Census provides comprehensive data on various demographic, social, and economic parameters.
 
• The first synchronous census in India was conducted in 1881, and since then, it has been conducted every decade.
 
• The Census data is crucial for planning and policy-making at various levels of government.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.
